plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $10, I should bid exactly $10 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values uniform on [0,49]. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies, since the payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not your own. Bidding above value risks overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $30 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. This is because if you win, you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid), so bidding higher than value risks overpaying, while bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. My value is $25, so I should bid exactly $25 to maximize expected profit.
